decisionMeaning: The nested predicate-Any membership scans are genuinely present. The actual retained fixture has two expected claims per site, only twelve declared theory rows, one real factory creation per row, and source-derived claim additions of 2 through 11. No concrete material elapsed/resource cost was observed or established from this source gate. No candidate is recommended. This is neither a measured no-gain result nor a false-positive or duplicate disposition, and it does not complete or alter any canonical campaign finding.

realWorkload.boundary: The declared test calls the real factory.CreateAsync(user), not an isolated Any/Contains helper. The factory's manager retrieval/capability calls are Moq setups returning the literal arrays; no real backing-store, HTTP, app, or large user database producer supplies these retained scans. The Poco user/role navigation collections start empty and are not the source of the configured returned arrays.

realWorkload.sourceDerivedAdditionFormula: 2 + E + 2*C + R*(2 + 4*RC), under the declared ordinary-mock/default-false stamp-capability assumption
realWorkload.sourceAssumption: SupportsUserSecurityStamp is an unconfigured virtual bool on an ordinary Mock<UserManager<T>> with no CallBase or stamp setup in the helper/target. Its standard default is false; the helper's IUserStore-only backing store would also fail the base manager's capability interface check. This source inference was not runtime-tested.
realWorkload.frequency: One factory.CreateAsync(user), one identity.Claims.ToList(), then the three two-element loops per declared row. If producer and prior assertions complete, each finding issues 24 membership queries across one full twelve-row matrix. No repeated workload or surrounding stress loop exists in this whole target. Actual runner discovery, executed rows, CI repeats, suite-wide frequency, and wall time remain unobserved.
realWorkload.sourceDerivedNotMeasuredBound: At most 22 predicate visits per site per declared row and a coarse summed full-scan bound of 148 per site over the declared matrix, conditional on preceding completion and the fixture assumptions. This is arithmetic over source cardinalities, not a simulated membership workload or an observed comparison/latency/allocation/savings result; Any can stop earlier.

contracts.typesAndMaterialization: Each expected collection is a two-element Claim[]. The scanned claims collection is a List<Claim>, created once by identity.Claims.ToList() before all three sites. The factory creates a new ClaimsIdentity and ClaimsPrincipal for each call; there is no shared lookup/index/cache in these sites.
contracts.equality: Each predicate compares c.Type == cl.Type && c.Value == cl.Value: case-sensitive ordinal string equality on both strings, Type first with && short-circuiting. It does not compare Claim object/reference identity and ignores issuer, original issuer, value type, subject, and claim properties. No Contains(Claim), ClaimsIdentity.HasClaim, case-normalized key, or reference-based equivalence may be substituted as an assumed contract.
contracts.values: All six expected type/value pairs are non-null literal Claim constructions. Admin and Local reuse Value1/Value2 but have different claim types; the pair, not value alone, identifies membership. User name, email and user ID are separate claims and do not inflate these expected arrays.
contracts.order: The source adds base ID/name, optional email/stamp, optional user claims, then the supplied roles in Admin/Local order, adding each role-name claim before that role's optional claims. The assertions ask membership, not collection order, but Any is first-match/short-circuiting and assertion failure ordering is user claims, admin claims, then local claims. The three source loops are distinct occurrences.
contracts.duplicates: The six explicit expected pairs are distinct. These Any assertions are existential, not multiset equality or exact claim-count assertions: extra matching duplicates would not fail a membership query. The factory does not introduce deduplication at these AddClaim/AddClaims call sites. No deduplication or assertion-strength change is proposed.
contracts.supportGates: User claims are added only when SupportsUserClaim; role names only when SupportsUserRole; admin/local claims require role support plus SupportsRoleClaims and a non-null role lookup. In the actual twelve rows, supportRoleClaims=true always has supportRoles=true. The four supportRoles=false/supportRoleClaims=true Boolean combinations are not declared tests and were not invented or characterized as passing.
contracts.exceptionsAndFailureOrder: The factory checks null user in CreateAsync and validates manager/options constructor inputs; the existing CreateIdentityNullChecks Fact covers optionsAccessor ArgumentException and user ArgumentNullException in source. Manager/base-store getters include disposed/unsupported-store/null checks, but the selected test mocks the retrievals: their real bodies are not asserted to run. Awaited producer/lookup failures would stop before these loops; a membership mismatch would stop at that Assert.Equal before later iterations/loops/VerifyAll. Eager alternate materialization or new assertions could change evaluation, exception or message boundaries, and none was authored.
contracts.noExtraCoverageClaim: Mixed-case, duplicate, null-claim, custom issuer/value-type, arbitrary role-count/claim-count, custom factory subclass, full sixteen-row matrix and framework/runtime implementation behavior were not executed or independently source-qualified.
